key_insight: Clinical AI diagnostic rankings can appear stronger when the reference knowledge base includes evidence from the test case’s own source publication, rather than reflecting generalization.
clinical_relevance: Trustworthy diagnostic benchmarks should separate patients, source-linked evidence, and time to avoid overstating performance relevant to clinical use.
method: Tracked 6,503 clinical cases across six HPO releases spanning October 2021–June 2026.
Identified when HPO first cited each case’s source publication as target-disease evidence.
Compared three diagnostic rankers before ingestion, after ingestion, and after removing source-linked assertions.
evidence_signal: In the confirmatory cohort, Resnik’s publication-weighted mean reciprocal rank rose from 0.26 before source ingestion to 0.84 afterward, then fell to 0.05 when source-linked assertions were removed; two additional rankers showed the same trajectory.
watch_item: These case-publication-based results flag benchmark contamination but do not establish performance in prospective clinical care.
paper_title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation
